strengths: Innovative perspective: Revisits audio deepfake detection (ADD) from a high-order interaction (HOI) standpoint, backed by an elegant information-theoretic analysis using O-information to distinguish between synergy and redundancy.

Well-crafted architecture: Effectively instantiates hypergraph learning via Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering, integrated with an attention-driven relational artifact amplification module and a class-aware prototype bank to guide initialization.

Extensive empirical validation: Evaluated across 13 different benchmark datasets, demonstrating competitive cross-dataset generalization and showing significant improvements over the strong Wav2Vec2-AASIST baseline in 11 out of 13 scenarios.

Insightful analysis and visualizations: Offers comprehensive visualizations of hyperedge cardinality, PCA of prototype banks, and segment-level similarities that clearly illustrate the mechanism and effectiveness of the proposed design.
weaknesses: Degradation under severe codec/channel distortion: The model's performance drops below the baseline on datasets with heavy audio compression (such as ASVspoof2021 LA and ASVspoof5), suggesting that codec distortions might corrupt the fine-grained high-order dependencies.

Increased computational complexity: The iterative Fuzzy C-Means clustering and hypergraph message passing introduce notable computational overhead, increasing inference latency and training time compared to standard graph networks.

Pipeline complexity and hyperparameter sensitivity: The prototype bank utilizes a complex progressive alignment process (soft and slot alignment) with multiple hyperparameters (e.g., fuzzifier, threshold, momentum, balance weights), which increases implementation complexity and potential sensitivity during tuning.

strengths: Grounds the motivation of audio deepfake detection (ADD) in high-order interactions (HOIs) using an information-theoretic framework (O-information), providing a novel perspective beyond traditional local and pairwise feature modeling.

Proposes a well-designed hypergraph framework (HyperPotter) integrating Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering and a memory-enhanced prototype bank to stabilize hyperedge initialization and capture cross-batch structural priors.
Conducts highly comprehensive evaluations across 13 diverse test sets, demonstrating notable relative EER reductions over the baseline in 11 sets.

Provides exceptional qualitative and quantitative analysis, including ablation studies, computational complexity/cost analysis, stability tests across random seeds, and insightful visualizations of synergy-redundancy ranks.
weaknesses: Introduces significant computational overhead: the Fuzzy C-Means clustering and hypergraph attention mechanism reduce the system's throughput significantly compared to the baseline (e.g., from 105.20 to 25.29 utt/s at batch size 64).

Suffers from performance degradation under severe codec compression and channel distortion (e.g., on ASVspoof2021 LA and ASVspoof5), which the authors hypothesize is due to these distortions masking fine-grained high-order spectral-temporal relations.

strengths: Novel Perspective: Investigating high-order interactions (HOIs) in audio deepfake detection via an information-theoretic framework (O-information) is highly original and theoretically grounded.

Extensive and Rigorous Evaluation: The paper evaluates the model on 13 diverse evaluation datasets spanning different languages, deepfake generation methods, and codecs. This is exceptionally thorough compared to standard evaluations in the literature.

Comprehensive Analysis: The inclusion of detailed ablation studies, sensitivity analyses (on cluster count, cardinality, and iterations), stability across multiple random seeds, and a thorough complexity/latency analysis provides deep insights into the behavior of the model.
Competitive Generalization: Demonstrates significant improvements over the strong Wav2Vec2-AASIST baseline on 11 out of 13 test sets with very minimal parameter addition (+0.03M).
weaknesses: Significant Computational Overhead: The reliance on Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering inside the neural network's forward pass introduces substantial training and inference latency (e.g., ~4x increase in inference latency at batch size 1). This limits the real-time applicability of the model.

High Complexity: The proposed framework contains a large number of moving parts (XLS-R, RawNet2, FCM, attention-driven artifact amplification, prototype banks with soft/slot-alignment, and EMA updates). This high complexity makes implementation, tuning, and reproduction challenging.

Vulnerability to Codec and Channel Noise: Performance degrades notably on datasets with severe compression/transmission distortions (ASVspoof 2021 LA and ASVspoof5). While codec augmentation is explored as a remedy, it severely impacts generalization on clean datasets (e.g., In-The-Wild EER degrades from 5.72% to 11.63% with +opus), showcasing a challenging trade-off.

strengths: The paper introduces a novel perspective to audio deepfake detection (ADD) by modeling high-order interactions (HOIs) through hypergraphs, grounded in an information-theoretic analysis (O-information theory).
The proposed prototype-guided hyperedge initialization mechanism effectively mitigates the typical instability and randomness associated with Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering.
The model is evaluated extensively on 13 different datasets, demonstrating strong generalization capability in most cross-domain scenarios compared to competitive baselines.
The ablation studies and visualization of hyperedge cardinality, dataset clustering, and segment-level relations are thorough and validate the core claims of capturing synergistic relationships.
weaknesses: The computational overhead of executing iterative Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering dynamically inside the network during both training and inference is not thoroughly evaluated or compared against other methods.
The proposed method shows a performance decline on datasets with strong distortions (such as 21LA and ASV2024), where it is outperformed by the pairwise baseline.

The framework introduces a large number of hyperparameters (e.g., fuzzifier m, threshold \tau, fusion weights \beta_1, \beta_2, momentum \mu, cluster size K, hyperedge degree D), making the optimization and tuning process complex.
The notation and alignment details in Section 5 are dense and relatively hard to parse, which impacts the readability of the prototype learning pipeline description.

strengths: Excellent use of information theory (O-information) to analyze and motivate the transition from pairwise graphs to hypergraphs to capture synergy-dominated high-order interactions (HOIs).

Integrating Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) based hypergraph attention with a class-aware prototype bank is technically sound and addresses the training instability/random-initialization issues of standard hypergraph construction.
Extensive experiments across 13 diverse datasets demonstrate strong generalization, particularly in challenging cross-domain settings (such as In-the-wild, FoR, and ADD2022).

The paper includes rich qualitative analyses, including hyperedge cardinality distributions, PCA visualizations, and similarity clustermaps, validating the physical meaning of the learned prototypes and HOIs.
weaknesses: The proposed method suffers from performance degradation under severe channel distortion (e.g., ASVspoof2021 LA and ASVspoof5) compared to the baseline, which limits its robustness in real-world transmission channels.

FCM is an iterative clustering algorithm (run for up to 5 iterations). The authors should discuss or quantify the computational complexity/overhead (training and inference speed) introduced by this iterative step, and clarify how gradients are backpropagated through the clustering process.
The overall framework is relatively complex, involving multiple nested modules (HAGNN, FCM, Relational Artifact Amplification, and a prototype bank with soft/slot-alignment and EMA).

strengths: The paper presents a solid information-theoretic motivation using O-information theory to justify the transition from pairwise relationships (redundancy-dominated) to high-order interactions (synergy-dominated) in audio deepfake detection.
Extensive evaluation across 13 diverse benchmark datasets, demonstrating strong generalization capability in cross-domain and cross-lingual scenarios.

The integration of Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering with a class-aware prototype bank is a well-reasoned solution to address the optimization instability commonly found in standard hypergraph neural networks.
Highly detailed manuscript that includes comprehensive ablation studies, parameter sensitivity analysis (hyperedge counts and degrees), and informative qualitative visualizations.
weaknesses: High architectural complexity: The framework combines several intricate components (including XLS-R, RawNet2, FCM, structural/feature similarity matrices, attention-driven amplification, similarity gating, soft/slot alignment, and EMA updates). This complexity makes the system difficult to reproduce, analyze, and tune.

Performance regressions on key datasets: The model suffers from notable degradation on ASVspoof2021 LA (3.94% EER vs. 2.48% for the baseline) and ASVspoof5 (16.04% EER vs. 13.38% for the baseline). Since robustness to real-world compression and channel distortion is crucial, this is a significant drawback.

Computational overhead: Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) is an iterative clustering algorithm. Running FCM on every batch/sample during training and inference likely introduces significant latency and computational costs, yet the paper lacks a detailed benchmark of training and inference times compared to baseline architectures.
Distracting terminology: The 'Harry Potter' theme ('Spell the Charm', 'HyperPotter') in the title and throughout the text feels gimmicky and detracts slightly from the scientific tone of the work.
